# dsh-continue-all
DSH Web UI plugin: one sidebar entry continues every session whose turn was left open by an unexpect
lugin: one sidebar entry continues every session whose turn was left open by an unexpected DSH exit.
When DSH is killed, crashes, or times out mid-turn, the turn stays open in the stored log. On the ne
xt resume the agent loop closes it as `interrupted`, and the session sits idle in the sidebar with a
failure notice. The usual fix is to open each affected session and press Continue. This plugin does
he usual fix is to open each affected session and press Continue. This plugin does that in one step.

For a local checkout, `link:/path/to/dsh-continue-all` works the same way.
## Use
The sidebar footer shows **Continue all**. Clicking it scans stored sessions, then lists the ones th
at stopped mid-turn. Confirming sends the literal prompt `continue` to each session in turn, through
the same session retention and `prompt(..., "queue")` path the composer uses. The dialog shows per-
session progress and failures.
Only sessions interrupted in the last 6 hours are selected by default. Older interrupted sessions ar
e listed behind an opt-in checkbox, so a batch cannot reach sessions from earlier crashes or abandon
ed work by accident.
Sessions are left out when they are:
ting for an approval or an answer.
Archived sessions stay archived. Unarchive one first if it should be continued.
## How detection works
The host half exposes `POST /api/continue-all/scan` on DSH's authenticated `/api` channel. It lists
visible stored sessions and reads each stored log. A session qualifies when its tail ends inside an
open turn, or when its last `turn/end` reason is `interrupted`. The response carries the time that t
urn stopped; the client uses it to separate the recent window from older sessions.
The scan caches its answer per persistence revision, so later scans read only logs that changed sinc
e the previous one. The first scan after a restart reads every stored log and can take a while on a
large history; the result is kept for the lifetime of the process. A warm scan starts shortly after
the host loads, so the first click usually finds it finished.
The client requires scan response version 2. After an update, restart `dsh web` once so the host and
client halves match; until then the dialog reports that the host half is out of date instead of sta
match; until then the dialog reports that the host half is out of date instead of starting anything.
Sessions whose logs cannot be read are skipped and logged on the host.

undary rules and stop times are tested without a live DSH.
